attacks.claim: The plan makes the closed-source, hosted-only Cirrus Cloud the single sync backend in 5.0 and archives the stride-server Docker image. This breaks the README/charter promise of self-hosting and data ownership for ~3,000 self-hosted instances, with no self-hostable path, no migration path, and no charter amendment or decision record. It is a planned one-way door.
attacks.evidence: "Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0 (planned for end of next year), after which Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived." / "the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service."

attacks.claim: A proprietary prebuilt binary under a commercial license is embedded in an MIT open-source app, with no analysis of license compatibility, redistribution rights, or whether the project can legally and philosophically carry it.
attacks.evidence: "The Cirrus client SDK is distributed as a prebuilt binary (iOS xcframework, Android AAR) under the Cirrus commercial license"

attacks.claim: Sync depends entirely on one vendor for client and server, with no exit path, fallback, or contingency if pricing, terms, or availability change. The free tier (100k devices) leaves only ~10% headroom over 90k users, and after 5.0 the ~3,000 self-hosters would also move onto Cirrus Cloud. Cost beyond the free tier is not modeled.
attacks.evidence: "free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier." ABSENT: exit/migration-off-Cirrus plan, cost model, pricing-change contingency.

attacks.claim: GPS tracks and workout data will be sent to a third-party processor with no stated data residency, processor terms/DPA, privacy-policy update, user notice, or consent. The beta cohort's real data also goes through it.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: data residency, DPA, privacy notice update, or consent flow; "Cirrus replicates to Cirrus Cloud when connectivity returns."

attacks.claim: Account deletion relies on a Cirrus admin API within 30 days with no verification that replicas or backups are purged, no failure handling, and no coverage of the on-device backup. The plan also does not say where the admin credentials live or which service holds them, so there is no defined authorization boundary. Self-hosted users have no stated deletion path.
attacks.evidence: "Account deletion removes the Cirrus user record and all synced records via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days."

attacks.claim: Downgrade to 3.x restores from the pre-migration backup, so anything recorded or edited in 4.x after migration is silently lost or reverted. The plan does not state or handle this reconciliation. Gating backup deletion on 'two successful syncs' also risks the backup never being cleaned up for poor-connectivity users.
attacks.evidence: "If migration fails or the user downgrades to 3.x, 3.x detects stride-backup-v3.db and restores from it; the backup is deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs"

attacks.claim: Migration has no verification step (record counts, checksums) before the backup is treated as safe. There is also no disk-space check, even though the backup copy roughly doubles on-device storage. Whether a restart after a kill re-copies or reuses the backup is unspecified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: validation/reconciliation step and disk-space check. "Migration is chunked (500 workouts per batch) and resumable if the app is killed mid-migration."

attacks.claim: The 90-day tombstone retention does not deliver the stated guarantee. A device offline longer than 90 days that still holds the workout can resurrect it after the tombstone is purged, and no handling is described. Per-field LWW on device-stamped HLCs also has no stated handling for clock skew or ties.
attacks.evidence: "Deletes are tombstones retained 90 days so an offline device cannot resurrect a deleted workout."

attacks.claim: Rollout gating and success metrics cannot detect the failures this project is meant to fix. The halt criterion is crash-free sessions only, the sync metric is client-reported on a small self-selected 500-person beta, and there is no server-side reconciliation, alerting, or sync spend/quota monitoring. Duplicates, data loss, or runaway cost could reach 100% undetected. No idempotency or retry design is given for the ambiguous-failure duplicate case.
attacks.evidence: "halting if crash-free sessions drop below 99.3%"; "Sync success rate (client-reported) >= 99.5% on beta cohort."

attacks.claim: The plan does not show that fixing the existing REST path (idempotent or chunked uploads with client IDs) was evaluated and rejected before adopting a proprietary vendor migration. It also has no user-facing communication about data moving to a third party.
attacks.evidence: "Adopt Cirrus Sync, a mobile offline-first sync SDK" vs. "Current REST sync uploads whole-workout blobs; a dropped connection mid-upload leaves a partial server row"

attacks.claim: The plan does not describe how the app authenticates to Cirrus Cloud or isolates records per user. It also does not describe TLS or certificate validation or credential handling for the retained custom-server REST path.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: Cirrus auth/token model, per-user isolation, TLS requirements for custom server URLs.

attacks.claim: A backend replacement, storage migration, conflict redesign, and legacy shim are bundled into one 5-week build for 3 contributors. The plan relies on an unprototyped vendor claim and a conflict spec held in an external document, so it is hard to verify or roll back in pieces.
attacks.evidence: "Week 1: Cirrus integration spike"; "Unit tests cover the 14 conflict scenarios enumerated in docs/sync-conflicts.md."
